messages:
priya: FYI new hire couldn't get the quickstart to succeed on their dev machine (Windows + VSCode Remote). curl -> 403, then after fiddling it worked. UI showed "Billing required" for their workspace even though billing is enabled.

priya: example from their WSL shell: ```
$ curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_redacted' https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "org_billing_needed",
  "message": "This workspace requires billing to make requests."
}
```

alex: did they copy the env var into the WSL environment or rely on the VSCode remote syncing? VSCode sometimes doesn't surface Windows envs into remote containers/sessions.

priya: they used the Windows system env panel to set REDWOOD_API_KEY and expected the remote to see it.

toni: we've seen this: Windows envs don't always propagate across the remote boundary, and corporate HTTP proxies can rewrite Authorization headers. two possible failure modes: header gets lost, or request reaches billing service as an unauthenticated call which triggers the billing-required UI state.

infra-bot: logs: "edge: received unauthenticated request from 10.23.45.67 (vs code-remote) - returning 403 org_billing_needed"

alex: try exporting the key inside WSL explicitly and re-run the sample app. also try `NO_PROXY=api.redwood.com` to bypass host proxy rewriting.

priya: verified steps: 
1) inside WSL: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_redacted`
2) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health`
response 200.

priya: sample Node quickstart also worked after exporting the env inside the remote. before that node failed with 403-based error: `Unhandled response: 403 org_billing_needed`. After exporting, first-call succeeded.

toni: action items:
- docs: add a short troubleshooting note in quickstart about Windows/VSCode Remote/WSL env propagation.
- devex: consider adding a short diagnostic in SDK/CLI when we see repeated unauthenticated requests from common remote agent fingerprints.
- infra: check whether the edge can include a hint when the request lacks Authorization and origin looks like a remote client.

docs-bot: opened DOCS-1287 for quickstart note; summary: "Windows: if using WSL/VSCode Remote, set REDWOOD_API_KEY inside the remote or set NO_PROXY for api.redwood.com"

priya: added onboarding checklist item for new hires who develop on Windows: "If using WSL or VSCode Remote, export REDWOOD_API_KEY in the remote shell or configure NO_PROXY for api.redwood.com."

alex: re: heuristics at the edge - be careful not to leak internal hints. maybe a simple trailing suggestion on 403: "If you're using Windows/WSL/remote dev tools, ensure your API key is exported inside the session or bypass host proxy (NO_PROXY)."

toni: I'll open INFRA-214 to evaluate. infra-bot: tagging relevant logs so we can search for similar incidents.

priya: resolved with user; they confirmed first successful call and quickstart sample app running. closing thread. :tada:
